claim: Graded sensory cancellation loses stability at short feedback delays (median critical delay 0.02 s; 100% failure at 140 ms)
caveat: toy model; failure threshold is a modeling choice

claim: All-or-none gating remains stable to a median critical delay of 0.20 s under the prespecified large-excursion criterion (19% failure at 140 ms)
caveat: criterion-dependent: ~60 ms under |omega|>50; no biological data

claim: Under the prespecified large-excursion criterion, gating on the delayed sensory estimate is more stable than gating on the current motor copy (0.20 s vs 0.11 s; 19% vs 75% failure at 140 ms)
caveat: difference disappears under |omega|>50; allnone_motor is a proxy for a motor copy

claim: Body time constant shifts the allnone boundary but not the graded-sensory boundary
caveat: only four body time constants sampled

claim: Noise does not remove the qualitative ordering
caveat: two seeds; noise amplitude is a modeling choice

claim: The extension is a new manipulation, not a replication of the source's supplementary delay comparison
caveat: source repository has no license; only equations were ported

claim: The manuscript does not claim that the fly uses any of the five variants
caveat: no new biological data

claim: Delayed visual feedback should destabilize graded cancellation before binary gating; gate release timing should matter
caveat: requires a delayed-feedback experiment

claim: 1 ms fine grid: median first failures at 18/15/10/110/200 ms for addition/graded_sensory/graded_motor/allnone_motor/allnone
caveat: three representative parameter sets; 1 ms only from 0 to 100 ms

claim: The ordering graded < gating is robust to the failure criterion, but the gating advantage and the allnone-vs-allnone_motor difference are criterion-dependent
caveat: post-hoc reclassification; no new simulations

claim: Halving the Euler step changes gating variants by <0.3% and fast-failing variants by 2-16% near divergence
caveat: single representative condition per model; no full DDE solver

claim: The zero-delay background-gain check does not reproduce the source's ranking; the source's behavioral result is motivation, not a validation
caveat: different stimulus protocol; single bar and single grating step

claim: The source's background ranking is recoverable with a near-zero gate threshold and a sub-unity EC gain; it is not generic to the fixed-gain model
caveat: scaled source parameters; constant-grating protocol; revised wording: not reproduced at a meaningful effect size (C12)

claim: EC gain determines whether graded cancellation is inert, harmful, or helpful: source gain 0.05 is inert; delayed sensory gain >=0.25 is harmful at 50 ms; current-oracle gain >=0.5 helps at 200 ms; gating is gain-invariant
caveat: four delays; 12 parameter sets; no noise in this sweep

claim: An adaptive MLP learns a higher gain (mean 0.38 to 1.06) and does not rescue delay: 100% failure at 50 ms versus 75% for no EC
caveat: step-wise MLP update, not the source's ODE-internal update

claim: Across learning rates 1e-5 to 1e-3 and three seeds, every adaptive rate reaches 100% failure by 100 ms; faster rates fail at 50 ms; no rate rescues stability
caveat: step-wise MLP update; four learning rates

claim: Linear stability around the target gives critical delays of 29-43 ms for addition/graded_sensory, 300 ms for graded_motor at gain 1.0, and 29 ms for allnone open-gate; gating and motor-copy benefits are large-signal/nonlinear
caveat: root tracking was unreliable at long delay; the 300 ms value was censoring, not a crossing

claim: A pre-plant-filter command copy does not rescue delay: graded command matches graded filtered (87.5% at 20 ms, 100% at 50-200 ms), and gate command matches gate filtered (0% at 20-100 ms, 75% at 140-200 ms); only the current-visual oracle has lower long-delay failure
caveat: command copy is still based on the delayed visual estimate; one seed, eight parameter sets; 6 s window

claim: A goal feedforward branch (instructed goal + current proprioception) rescues delay: gate goal at ff_gain >= 0.5 has 0% failure from 20 to 200 ms at 6 s and 10 s windows; graded goal at ff=1.0 matches the current-visual oracle (0.625-0.75)
caveat: goal is instructed and shares amplitude/onset with the stimulus; upper bound, not a biological mechanism; current proprioception assumed available

claim: The feedforward rescue requires current self-state: delaying the goal itself changes nothing, while replacing current proprioception with delayed values raises gate goal failure to 0.75-1.0 and makes it worse than gate filtered at 100 ms
caveat: two visual delays, one seed, eight parameter sets; 6 s window

claim: The command-copy and feedforward conclusions hold across three seeds (24 parameter-seed combinations per cell): graded command equals graded filtered identically; gate goal ff>=0.5 is 0% at every delay in every seed
caveat: gain 1.0 only; noise SD 1e-13

claim: Integrating the adaptive MLP weights as ODE states reproduces the step-wise update: 96/96 paired runs agree on failure classification and failure time; trajectories agree until chaotic amplification in runs that diverge anyway
caveat: forward Euler only; source solver semantics not reproduced

claim: The earlier long-delay gating advantage was a finite-window artifact: gate filtered at 140 ms fails 3/16 at 2.5 s, 11/16 at 6 s, 12/16 at 10 s
caveat: 2 seeds, 8 parameter sets; noise included

claim: The 100 ms gating advantage depends on the velocity-nonlinearity shape: 0% under clip and unclipped, 75% under smooth for gate filtered
caveat: gate unfiltered shows 6.2% under clip/unclipped at 100 ms

claim: Short-delay (20-50 ms) gating is 0% for gate filtered across thresholds 0.01-0.5 and both V treatments; gate unfiltered matches except threshold 0.5 clip at 50 ms (25%) and 100 ms (62.5% vs 37.5%)
caveat: threshold sweep used dt=2e-4 (step-halving check in C11)

claim: The adaptive comparison across three update rules gives mean gain 0.51 to 1.05 (source-style) versus 0.22 to 0.40 (signed gradient); failure stays 50% at 20 ms and 100% at 50 ms+ in all modes
caveat: step-wise update verified equivalent to ODE-internal form (C22)

claim: Gate goal at ff=1.0 stays at 0% failure through 500 ms at a 10 s window; ff=0.5 degrades beyond 200 ms (12.5% at 250/300 ms, 62.5% at 400 ms, 50% at 500 ms)
caveat: 1 seed, 8 parameter sets; 10 s window

claim: On a 10 ms grid (0-250 ms, 6 s), first delay with failure >= 0.5 is 20 ms (graded filtered), 10 ms (graded goal), 130 ms (gate filtered), and not reached for gate goal ff=1.0
caveat: 1 seed, 8 parameter sets

claim: Noise robustness: conclusions unchanged for torque-noise SD from 0 to 1e-11 N m; only gate filtered at 100 ms moves (0% to 12.5%)
caveat: 1 seed, 8 parameter sets; 5 delays

claim: Across 4 inertias x 3 drags x 2 grating gains x 8 delays, gate goal ff=1.0 fails in none of the 24 body-gain combinations at any delay 20-400 ms; gate filtered rises from 12.5% at 20 ms to 66.7% at 200 ms+ (averaged)
caveat: 1 seed per cell; 6 s window

claim: Example trajectories at 200 ms and 10 s: addition and graded filtered diverge to 1e8-1e13 rad; gate filtered and gate goal stay bounded (final heading 1.27 and 1.11 rad)
caveat: single parameter set and seed

claim: Goal-mismatch robustness: gate goal ff=1.0 stays at 0% for goal amplitudes 45-75 degrees and time constants 0.05-0.20 s; ff=0.5 fails 12.5% only at 45 degrees undershoot, 200 ms
caveat: 1 seed, 8 parameter sets; onset fixed

claim: Failure-criterion sensitivity: on 3 representative parameter sets, halving the angular-velocity threshold (100 to 50 rad/s) moves the gating critical delay from 200 to 56 ms (gate filtered) and 110 to 58 ms (gate unfiltered); continuous variants stay 10-18 ms
caveat: reclassification of P3 fine-grid data; 3 parameter sets

claim: Goal onset decoupling: moving the goal onset from 0.3 to 0.8 s (bar fixed at 0.5 s) changes no failure rate; gate goal stays 0% at 100 and 200 ms, graded goal stays 75%
caveat: 1 seed, 8 parameter sets; amplitude still matched

claim: No-goal damping control: pure derivative feedback on current angular velocity rescues the gate (0% at 200 ms for gains >= 1e-11) without any target information; the graded family improves only partially (50-62.5% at the highest gain)
caveat: 1 seed, 8 parameter sets; three damping gains; damping matched by scale, not by RMS torque

claim: Self-state freshness dose-response: gate goal stays at 0% for self-state sample ages up to 30 ms (visual 100 ms) or 10 ms (visual 200 ms) and degrades to the gate filtered level by 40 ms (100 ms) / 30 ms (200 ms); graded goal reaches 100% by 10-20 ms of age
caveat: 1 seed, 8 parameter sets; lags up to 200 ms; 6 s window

claim: Equal-information observer baseline: a second-order Taylor estimate of current state reconstructed from the delayed observation alone does not substitute for fresh self-state (gate goal predicted: 50% failure at 50 ms, 100% at 100 ms+), while true current state stays at 0% at every delay
caveat: only a trivial Taylor estimator; a perfect internal-model observer is an untested upper bound; 1 seed, 8 parameter sets

claim: Classifier robustness: the instantaneous peak criterion and a 10 ms sustained criterion disagree on 0 of 720 trajectories; label flips across seed/noise/dt localize entirely to gate filtered at 100-140 ms (drag 1e-11, k_opto 5e-11), so boundary-region failure rates are ensemble quantities over seed, noise, and integration-step perturbations
caveat: 5 representative conditions, not a re-labeling of historical rounds; dwell 10 ms is a modeling choice; manuscript criterion unchanged (instantaneous peak)

claim: A delayed-only forward-model observer does not rescue delay: the Smith-style estimator fails in 100% of parameter sets at >=100 ms and 50% at 50 ms, with exact internal model and with 10% drag/inertia mismatch
caveat: internal model omits the delay in its feedback loop (naive forward model); DDE-aware observer untested

claim: Matched-budget instantaneous classical PD without gating fails 38-62% at all delays 50-200 ms; W1 shows the failure is entirely attributable to the ungated delayed grating loop (C47), so this row records the unfixed-comparator result only
caveat: interpretation superseded by C47; PD untuned

claim: Gating has an independent contribution WITHIN the delayed-self-state architecture: disabling the gate inside gate_goal raises failure to 88-100% (C49), and at matched instantaneous state and goal branch gated is 0% while ungated graded_goal is 62-75% failure
caveat: model-level statement only

claim: Fly-level benchmark reproduction of the Tanaka/Clark public dataset: Mi4 matches the authors' precomputed traces exactly (r=1.0); T4/T5 experimental epochs r>=0.94; LPTC shows no consistent stationary suppression across five cell types, matching the published claim
caveat: pipeline validation on same-source data; not independent biological evidence

claim: Behavioral graded-vs-gated model selection on the contrast sweep is INCONCLUSIVE_BY_RESOLUTION at n=19: nested LFO-CV delta RMSE=-0.091, parametric-bootstrap p=0.534, minimum detectable |delta|=0.454; the exploration coarse-grid gap vanished under refined fitting
caveat: resolution-limited; no directional claim

claim: Under identical visual stimulus structure, past motor history adds held-out predictive information for HS membrane potential beyond a visual-history model (9/12 animals positive; median dR2=+0.056; exact sign-flip p=0.0503; CI95 crosses zero; owner stage-gate pass D12 with numbers on record)
caveat: prediction information only, not efference-copy source; cross-animal scale mismatch dominates absolute R2

claim: A naive state-dependent perturbation test is defeated by generic behavioral autocorrelation: pre-pulse state predicts yaw responses around real pulses (median dLL +28.1) but equally around random pseudo-pulses in unstimulated controls (+20.1)
caveat: n=6 intervention animals; capacity control not implemented in this round (disclosed)

claim: A residual pipeline that removes the state-to-behavior autocorrelation map (learned only from non-pulse epochs) shrinks the artifact floor to +6.88 while a consistent positive excess remains (6/6 animals, median +8.57, p=1/64), below the preregistered 3x specificity threshold; perturbation-specific state dependence NOT established
caveat: all three negative controls implemented; candidate signal recorded for expandable-n datasets

claim: Gated classical control rescues fully: instantaneous classical PD with allnone-style grating gating (pd_gate) fails 0 of 8 parameter sets at every delay 50-200 ms, and instantaneous PD with the grating pathway removed is also at 0% across a p_gain sweep of 0.5x-5x — the classical comparator failure of C40 was caused by the ungated delayed grating loop
caveat: fast feedback path is classical PD; the non-classical-fast-path framing of earlier drafts is retracted

claim: An observer whose internal feedback loop embeds the transport delay (smith_dde, interval innovation correction) fails in 8 of 8 parameter sets at ALL delays 50-200 ms with exact parameters and with 10% drag/inertia mismatch, while gate_goal stays at 0%
caveat: interval hard correction, not an Artstein-type reduction; the delay-free-prediction upper bound remains untested

claim: Gate ablation within the same architecture: disabling the grating gate inside gate_goal raises failure to 0.88-1.00, while triggering the gate on |F_bar| alone preserves 0% failure at all delays (goal-augmented trigger unnecessary)
caveat: one seed, eight parameter sets

claim: Delay-assignment robustness: with current psi/omega available to the delayed bar and grating pathways, addition, graded filtered, and gate filtered all reach 0% failure at every delay 50-200 ms (delayed reference addition fails 100%) — the continuous-variant instability is manufactured by withholding self-state, and gating is conditional on that withholding
caveat: single seed, eight parameter sets; stimulus angles remain delayed

claim: Boundary multi-seed check: gate_goal ff=1 remains at 0% failure for delays 250-500 ms across three seeds, and gate filtered stays at 0.75; long-delay and phase boundary claims are seed-robust
caveat: three seeds only; six-second window

claim: Revised necessity picture: fresh current self-state in the closing feedback loop is the fundamental necessary ingredient (classical PD with current state suffices; delayed-only estimation at every tested order fails; delayed pathways with current self-state need no gating), and gating of the delayed sensory pathway is the substitute architecture when that pathway cannot receive current self-state
caveat: within this model class and the enumerated architectures; not a formal necessity proof

claim: Injection-recovery validation of the pseudo-pulse/residual pipeline: injected state-dependent effects are recovered monotonically with a detection threshold at beta=8 (paired sign-flip p=0.020) and robust recovery at beta>=16 (p<=5e-5); effects at beta<=4 (<1% residual variance) are undetectable at five sessions
caveat: additive injection on control sessions; five sessions operating point

claim: Transfer to artificial delayed control tasks: fresh-state LQR (reference delayed) shows 0% failure at every delay 0-600 ms across three randomized task families, while delayed-observation LQR and velocity extrapolation cross 50% failure at 50-200 ms; stacking the delayed-state term ungated degrades the fresh family to 150-400 ms critical delays
caveat: linearizations with Gaussian noise; fresh family privileged by construction (proprioception analog); observer result is practical-under-noise, not impossibility

claim: The delay-embedding forward observer improves over naive delayed baselines on artificial tasks (critical 150-300 ms) but never reaches the fresh-state family, and 10% parameter mismatch does not consistently help; zero-delay C/F identity verified
caveat: deterministic noiseless setting could reconstruct exactly; practical claim only
